Fig. 37 · Third kind · loses nothing, so never stops

The frictionless pendulum

Sheet
37 of 56
Group
The third kind
Motion

The claim

Hang a pendulum on a perfect pivot, pump every molecule of air out of the jar, and let go. With nothing to carry energy away, each swing rises as high as the last, for ever.

Why it stops

No pump removes every molecule and no pivot is perfect. Leftover gas drags on the bob, the pivot rubs, the rod flexes and warms. Each swing ends a little lower than the one before. Careful engineering stretches the run from minutes to days. Even then, drawing any work from the motion slows it down, so a machine of this kind can never be an engine.
